articles.title: Veterans ask federal judge to block Trump's arch unless Congress approves it
articles.summary: With the Trump administration signaling that work on the triumphal arch near Arlington National Cemetery could begin two weeks from Thursday, opponents of the project urged a federal judge to issue an order blocking the construction unless it is authorized by lawmakers. The request for a preliminary injunction comes a day after the Justice Department filed notice with a federal judge indicating that construction on the arch could begin on Nov. 5, immediately after the National Capital Planning Commission is set to grant its final approval of the project. Judge Tanya Chutkan had previously ordered that the government must give at least 14 days' notice before starting work on the arch. Wednesday's notice would keep with that timeframe. Harrison Design/U.S. Commission of Fine Arts - PHOTO: A rendering of the ‘triumphal arch,” that the Trump administration is planning to build near Arlington National Cemetery. The Vietnam-era veterans who have brought a lawsuit against the arch asked Chutkan to step in so that the administration can't "render the arch a fait accompli before this Court has made a final determination whether Defendants' project is unlawful." Triumphal Arch final plans submitted by Interior Department to National Capital Planning Commission The veterans' filing accuses the administration of having "barreled ahead, doing site testing, drawing architectural plans, and seeking approvals from commissions populated by friends of the administration." All the while, the filing says, the Trump administration has "failed to obtain (or even to seek) approval from the one body that, by law, must authorize the project: Congress." The administration argues that the bill signed by President Calvin Coolidge in 1925 providing for the construction of Memorial Bridge also authorizes the arch, because the initial plan called for columns at the end of the bridge. Opponents describe the administration's argument as "entirely untethered" from the text of that 1925 law. Federal preservation agency says it's 'terminating' required consultation with local officials on Trump's arch Trump's proposal would put the 250-foot arch in a traffic circle across the Potomac River from the Lincoln Memorial at the foot of the national cemetery. It currently faces legal challenges by the veterans and preservationists. The administration acknowledged in September that the arch would cause "adverse effects" on the setting and views along the rive, but those impacts "cannot be fully avoided" because the arch's location is "central to the undertaking." articles.title: Supreme Court sides with Republicans in New Hampshire student ID voting fight
articles.summary: WASHINGTON – The Supreme Court said New Hampshire can fully enforce a ban on voters using student IDs as a form of identification at the polls next month, a win for the Republican Party's effort to tighten voting procedures. The court on Oct. 22 agreed to pause a lower court’s ruling that a student ID is among the forms of identification that may be considered by poll workers if the voter lacks an approved government-issued ID. The state's U.S. Senate race is among the contests that will decide whether Republicans keep control of that chamber after the midterm elections. The Republican National Committee had backed the state's unsuccessful emergency appeal to the Supreme Court . New Hampshire, controlled by Republicans, is among several states that have banned registered voters from using a student ID to verify their identity at the polls. A voting-rights group challenged the change as discrimination against younger voters and as an unconstitutional burden on their right to vote. A federal judge in New Hampshire declined to block enforcement of the law as the case is litigated. But the judge also said the new law had not changed the fact that a poll worker may accept or reject a student ID as a valid form of identification on a case-by-case basis through the state’s "safety-valve" provision. New Hampshire Secretary of State David Scanlan asked the Supreme Court to intervene. Scanlan, a Republican, said the judge's Oct. 2 order injected uncertainty into the state’s voting procedures less than three weeks before the election. He also said the judge wrongly interpreted the state's law. Coalition for Open Democracy, the group challenging the law, said the judge correctly concluded that state officials failed to identify "any security or integrity concerns specific to student ID cards and why they are unique among other non-governmental forms of identification" that are allowed on a case-by-case basis. The judge also found that the change had already kept one student from voting and could affect more because young voters may not have the government-issued IDs that are automatically accepted. In the brief and unsigned opinion, the Supreme Court pointed to its previous rulings that federal courts should not alter rules on the eve of an election. Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson was the only justice to publicly disagree with that decision. She said the federal judge had not changed the rules but only corrected the secretary of state's misinterpretation of them. "I respectfully dissent because − even, and perhaps especially, when an election is looming − I would not disturb aclearly justifiable federal-court order issued to ensure that the public receives accurate information about a State'selectoral processes," she wrote. articles.title: First-of-its-kind cancer vaccine cuts risk of melanoma returning by 42% in major trial
articles.summary: WASHINGTON (AP) — A first-of-its-kind cancer vaccine is significantly reducing the chances that melanoma patients’ tumors come back, according to results of a major study released Thursday by drugmakers Moderna and Merck. The vaccine was custom-brewed for each patient to match their tumor. Adding it to a standard post-surgery treatment reduced by 42% the risk of melanoma returning two years after surgery, according to the most advanced study to date of this new strategy for fighting cancer. “The field has been looking for a win and I think this one is a big one,” said Dr. Hussein Tawbi of MD Anderson Cancer Center in Houston, one of the researchers in the international study. The vaccine, called intismeran, is made with the same Nobel Prize-winning mRNA technology that was behind COVID-19 vaccines. Experimental personalized cancer vaccines made with mRNA and some other approaches also are being tested against other types of cancer including lung, kidney and pancreatic. Experts not involved with the new study say its success bolsters the field. “This is a new frontier,” said Karen Knudsen, CEO of the Parker Institute, which helps fund cancer immunotherapy research. “It’s a big step forward for science, for oncology, because this vaccine will apply to many different cancers,” said Dr. Michael Atkins, deputy director of Georgetown University’s Lombardi Comprehensive Cancer Center. Moderna and Merck had announced in August that the late-stage trial of intismeran was successful but the detailed results were set to be released Saturday at a meeting of the European Society of Medical Oncology in Madrid. Some of the data was leaked publicly late Thursday, prompting a full release ahead of the weekend's scientific presentation. Most people think of vaccines as preventing an infection, like measles or whooping cough. There are already two cancer-preventing vaccines, the HPV and hepatitis B shots that block infection from those tumor-causing viruses. And research is underway to prevent some types of inherited cancer such as Lynch syndrome-caused colorectal cancer. But a personalized vaccine designed to block surgically-removed cancer from returning is very different. For the intismeran study, scientists hunted gene mutations unique to each patient’s tumor, mutations that create proteins which shouldn’t be in the body unless those cancer cells start to grow again. The custom vaccine — nine doses given three weeks apart — teaches the patient’s immune system to watch out for and attack those so-called neoantigens. How did it work? The study included more than 1,100 people with high-risk melanoma that was surgically removed. Everyone was given the standard follow-up therapy: Merck’s immunotherapy named Keytruda. The participants were randomly assigned to also receive custom-brewed vaccine doses or a placebo. Two years later, 82% of the people in the vaccine group were still living without a recurrence of their cancer compared to 70% who had gotten standard Keytruda alone. The trial is continuing to track participants’ longer-term outcomes. In 2024, Tony Hout joined the vaccine trial at MD Anderson after seeking care for a spot on his ear that had been bleeding intermittently and wouldn’t fully heal. Doctors recognized melanoma and during surgery discovered it had started to spread. “I want to make sure I’m doing everything I can to be here for my family,” said Hout, 62, who has since moved to Cayuga, Indiana, and travels back to Houston every few months for a study check-up. Scans this week showed he’s still cancer-free. The vaccine’s side effects were mainly the sore arm, fatigue and other reactions typical of mRNA coronavirus vaccination, MD Anderson's Tawbi said. Moderna and Merck are talking with regulatory authorities about next steps for seeking approval of the vaccine. Customized medicines generally are very expensive. The drugmakers aren’t discussing what such a cancer vaccine might cost. But Moderna President Stephen Hoge said the company’s special cancer vaccine manufacturing facility in Massachusetts is providing doses for thousands of people enrolled in multiple studies underway internationally. Hoge said it takes a few days to brew the vaccine but the whole process, starting with analyzing the tumor genetics to come up with what is essentially a recipe for each patient, can take roughly six weeks, sometimes more. Meanwhile, the melanoma patients had already started their standard Keytruda, a different kind of immunotherapy. Moderna shares dropped 18% Thursday after the study’s full results were made public, but they remained more than 200% higher than they were in late August before investors were first told of the initial results. ___ The Associated Press’ health and science coverage receives financial support from the AP Fund for Journalism and private foundations. articles.title: Pastor Adam Hamilton could be Kansas's 1st Democratic senator since the Depression
articles.summary: When it comes to picking senators, no state is nearly as consistent as Kansas. The last Democrat to win there, a former county attorney named George McGill, was elected in 1932. Kansas's other senator, a Republican incumbent, won reelection in 1936. McGill lost to a Republican in 1938. And Kansas has been sending Republicans to the U.S. Senate ever since. That's a 90-year winning streak. But the composition of Kansas's Senate delegation could change on Nov. 3 — and with it, Republican control of the chamber as a whole. To the surprise of pretty much the entire political world, first-term GOP incumbent Roger Marshall is currently locked in a too-close-to-call contest with megachurch-pastor-turned-rookie-candidate Adam Hamilton — a former Republican who considered running as an independent before deciding to seek the Sunflower State's Democratic nomination. Hamilton, 61, is one of several heartland Democrats or Democratic-leaning independents who are giving Senate Republicans a run for their money in ruby-red states that President Trump won by double-digit margins in 2024 (including Texas, Iowa, Nebraska and even South Carolina ). He describes himself as " a liberal conservative and a conservative liberal ." "I'm not somebody who favors the Socialist Party," Hamilton said Wednesday night during a debate against Marshall. "I'm somebody who stands in the middle. I'm going to try to work for all Kansans, Republicans, independents and Democrats." Here's everything you need to know about one of the key figures of the 2026 midterms. Yahoo Who is Adam Hamilton? In some ways, Hamilton is similar to James Talarico, the Democratic Senate nominee in Texas , who is equally unapologetic about his Christian faith. But where Talarico has studied at seminary on the side — his main gig has been serving in the Texas House of Representatives — Hamilton is a bona fide church leader. Born in 1964 and raised in the Kansas City suburb of Prairie Village, Hamilton didn't go to church regularly as a child. His parents were teenage high school dropouts when they had him; they divorced by the time he was a teenager. Hamilton started drinking and taking drugs in seventh grade; two years later he got clean and started attending Pentecostal services on the recommendation of a door-to-door evangelist. Before long, Hamilton was heading up the church's youth group; he married a fellow attendee a week after high school graduation. Eventually, he earned a bachelor's degree in pastoral ministry from Oral Roberts University in Tulsa and a Master of Divinity from Southern Methodist University in Dallas. In 1990 — when Hamilton was just 25 — his United Methodist denomination tapped him to start a church for nonchurchgoers in suburban Kansas City. Worshippers initially met in the small chapel of a local funeral home. Today, Hamilton's United Methodist Church of the Resurrection is the largest United Methodist congregation in the U.S., with an average weekly attendance of about 25,000 people online, on television and across its nine area campuses. Its Christmas Eve offering, which is devoted to mission work, has topped $2 million . Hamilton has also written more than 30 books that have together sold millions of copies; his video-based lessons are used in Sunday school classes nationwide. In 2013, he preached at the National Prayer Service after President Barack Obama's second inauguration. Three years later, Obama appointed Hamilton to his Advisory Council on Faith-Based and Neighborhood Partnerships. Hamilton was registered as a Republican as recently as 2020; when he was first considering a 2026 Senate bid, he formed an exploratory committee as an independent. At the time he told his congregation — "a nearly equal mix of Republicans, Democrats and Independents," according to the Associated Press — that he could "bridge partisan divides in a highly polarized political climate" (as the AP put it). "Every week, it seemed there was another news story in the last year where I would find myself shaking my head and thinking, we have to do better," the self-described fifth-generation Kansan told the AP. But Hamilton was persuaded to run as a Democrat so as not to split the anti-Marshall vote in the general election. He wound up massively outraising his Democratic primary opponents and winning the party's Aug. 4 primary by more than 20 percentage points . What does Hamilton stand for? In college, Hamilton chose not to become a Pentecostal preacher because the denomination felt too black and white. In contrast, Methodism struck him as a thinking person's church, he told a local Kansas City paper in 2002 . "It seemed to me there was some gray in the world," Hamilton explained. "It is OK if you have doubts. It's OK if you have questions. We don't have to check our brains at the door." He now says he is an "independent-minded Democrat" who is "going to work across the aisle." At the Wednesday debate, Hamilton criticized Marshall for supporting the Trump administration's least-popular policies — tariffs, the war in Iran, immigration raids in farm country — while trying to distance himself from national Democrats. He called former President Joe Biden's immigration policy a "disaster," for instance, and promised not to "support Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader if the Democrats [were] to control the Senate." When asked about transgender girls playing women's sports, Hamilton said he would not want his 12-year-old granddaughter competing against people assigned male at birth. "It's not a fair fight," he argued. Hamilton, left, and Republican Sen. Roger Marshall participate in a debate at WDAF TV in Kansas City, Mo. on Oct. 21, 2026. Charlie Riedel/AP via AP At times, Hamilton — who reminded the audience that he has "been a pastor for the last 38 years" and has "not been a senator" — struggled to provide specifics on issues such as farm subsidies, the Social Security wage cap and AI regulation, according to the New York Times . But Hamilton's general approach — his focus on "decency," affordability and "bringing people together" — has its roots in his ministry. Following the recent surge of federal immigration agents to Minneapolis, he cited on his podcast an Old Testament verse that commands Israelites to treat foreigners with love and fairness. In April, he said that he had voted against a state constitutional amendment that would have cleared the way for tougher abortion restrictions, arguing lawmakers should not be "the ethicists and the spiritual guides" for women (even as he lamented that his mother considered having an abortion when she was pregnant with him). And he has criticized Republican cuts to federal safety-net programs such as food stamps and Medicaid. "I just want to know, when did it become 'woke' to care for your neighbor?" Hamilton asked the AP , claiming that "Marshall would call [Jesus] 'woke'" if he were alive today. How could Hamilton perform in the midterms? Hamilton's local prominence, fundraising prowess, "centrist" message and skill on the stump have made this year's Kansas Senate contest very competitive. ("No one has more practice at extemporaneous talking than a megachurch pastor," the Times noted.) Marshall leads by 1 percentage point in the most recent poll to be released — but it's the only survey conducted over the last month that shows the Republican candidate ahead. The rest (save one tie) give Hamilton a slight edge (between 1 and 5 percentage points). Both candidates have faced controversy. Marshall has pushed back on reports that he sued hundreds of patients over unpaid medical bills during his decades-long career as an obstetrician-gynecologist, calling the allegations "blatant lies." And Hamilton has admitted he made a "mistake" by failing to bar a volunteer who had previously been accused of sexual abuse in 2005 from going on a retreat where he allegedly abused another boy. "I was actually preaching that weekend at Church of the Resurrection, and I did not sign off on him going back. I should have checked to make sure that he wasn't going back," Hamilton said during Wednesday's debate. "That was a mistake on my part. But I will tell you, when he was investigated the next year, we forbade him from working with youth or children anymore. He left our church angry and upset. And again, we played a critical role several years later in getting him arrested and convicted." Kansas hasn't sent a Democratic senator to Washington, D.C., since the Dust Bowl days — a conservative bent that's also reflected in its heavily Republican state legislature and the fact that it has voted Republican in every presidential election since 1940 except for Lyndon B. Johnson's 1964 landslide. But the state has elected two Democratic governors in recent years — Kathleen Sebelius (2003-2009) and term-limited incumbent Laura Kelly (2019-2027) — and there is a tradition of ticket-splitting that goes back even further. (Since 1957, neither major political party has held the Kansas governor's mansion for longer than eight consecutive years.) Could Hamilton benefit from that sort of checks-and-balances heterodoxy on Nov. 3? It's possible. In Wednesday's debate, Marshall embraced the Trump agenda and explicitly told viewers that "if you want [it] to continue, you need to come out, because we delivered on those things." But even in Kansas, 53% of likely voters currently disapprove of how the president is handling his job . The fate of Hamilton's campaign, and perhaps his party's hopes of winning the Senate, will turn on whether he can convince those voters to cast their ballots for him on Election Day — even if they haven't voted for a Democrat in a long, long time. articles.title: MAHA leader exits Trump admin. after reported frustrations over food policy
articles.summary: Calley Means, senior advisor at Health and Human Services (HHS) and co-founder of TrueMed, at the Semafor World Economy Summit during the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Spring meetings in Washington, D.C., on April 25, 2025. —Kent Nishimura—Bloomberg/Getty Images Calley Means , one of the key figures in the Make America Healthy Again (MAHA) movement, said on Thursday that he was stepping down from his role as a senior health adviser in the Trump Administration. In a post on X , Means said that he was resigning “with tremendous respect” for President Donald Trump and Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. “They laid out a vision of combatting the entrenched, dark forces in DC that profit from Americans getting sick,” Means said. “More policy and cultural change has happened around these goals in the past 2 years than any time in history—and I know this movement is just getting started.” News outlets including the New York Times and POLITICO , citing anonymous sources with knowledge of the situation, have reported that Means was becoming increasingly frustrated because he felt that there was little movement on issues central to the MAHA agenda—for instance, on the issue of defining and regulating ultraprocessed foods. Means, who was pivotal in coordinating an alliance between Kennedy and Trump during the 2024 election cycle, has championed the Administration's food-policy agenda, including efforts to persuade manufacturers to stop using artificial food dyes in their products and to restrict the purchase of soda with Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits in some states. In his social media post, Means heralded those actions, as well as his efforts to reform dietary guidelines and his push for research into psychedelic medications. “It was an honor to advocate for MAHA moms in the administration,” Means said. Means is the latest figure in the Trump Administration, and specifically in the Department of Health and Human Services, to resign or be ousted from their role over the past year. In May, Dr. Marty Makary stepped down as the head of the Food and Drug Administration amid pressure from within and outside of the Trump Administration. Last year, the White House fired Susan Monarez as director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. In April, Trump withdrew his nomination of MAHA leader Dr. Casey Means —Calley Means’ sister—for the position of U.S. Surgeon General after the nomination failed to garner enough support in the Senate. articles.title: Meta struck an unusual deal to keep Mark Zuckerberg from leaving California
articles.summary: Meta Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg has made a deal with the firm's board allowing him to sell or transfer up to 20% of the company's new Class C stock so that his voting majority doesn't decrease even if he has to pay the billionaire tax. (Nic Coury / Associated Press ) Meta’s Chief Executive Mark Zuckerberg has wielded enormous power over the social media empire he built more than two decades ago, leading the California juggernaut through major scandals, scrutiny and technological shifts. But the 42-year-old tech mogul considered leaving the state because he feared that a ballot measure to impose a one-time 5% tax on the assets of California billionaires could reduce the amount of control he has over Meta, a recent regulatory filing shows. Meta’s board struck a deal so he would stay in California. Meta is the parent company of Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp. The filing highlights how one of the world’s wealthiest people, whose net worth totals more than $200 billion, is bracing for the possibility that California voters pass Proposition 40, a wealth tax proposal that would primarily be used to fund healthcare. Although supporters say the fear that billionaires will flee the state are overblown, the ultrawealthy have made moves to potentially avoid paying the tax or are funding campaigns to defeat it. Read more: Your guide to Proposition 40: California's billionaire tax proposal Zuckerberg’s influence over Meta is partly tied to how the company structures its stock. Zuckerberg holds roughly 60% of voting power over Meta even though he only owns about 13% of the company’s total shares. Meta has a dual-class share structure, dividing the stock into Class A shares with one vote each and Class B shares with 10 votes each. Zuckerberg holds a large amount of Class B stock, which gives him majority control over company decisions. If the wealth tax proposal passes, Zuckerberg is worried that it could reduce his voting power, according to the filing. The tech executive makes an annual salary of $1, so most of his wealth is linked to his stake in Meta. If he had to sell his Class B shares to pay the tax, that would reduce his voting majority in the company, according to the filing. In September, he told Meta’s board that he planned to list his Palo Alto home for sale, pressuring board members to find a solution. On Wednesday, Meta announced a new class of stock with no voting rights called Class C that would take effect in January. As part of the deal, Zuckerberg could sell or transfer up to 20% of Class C stock so his voting majority doesn’t decrease even if he has to pay the tax. “Mr. Zuckerberg’s continued leadership role in our Company, and his continuing presence at the Company’s headquarters in California, is critical at this current inflection point for the Company and the tech industry in order to continue to provide value-maximization for all shareholders,” the filing said. Since the company’s public debut, its share price has risen more than 1,700%, outperforming the S&P 500. In Meta’s third-quarter earnings call Wednesday, Chief Financial Officer Susan Li said creating a new class of nonvoting stock benefits the company in various ways, including “capital raising, employee compensation, acquisitions, other general corporate purposes.” “We believe this share class will maintain our founder-led structure. It will expand our funding tools and give us flexibility to invest behind the unprecedented momentum we’re seeing across every part of our business driven by AI,” she said. Meta has roughly 66,700 workers globally. Its sprawling headquarters is in Menlo Park. Some billionaires such as Anduril co-founder Palmer Luckey, Ripple co-founder Chris Larsen and Google co-founder Sergey Brin have opposed the wealth tax proposal. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, on the other hand, has said he doesn’t mind paying more taxes. The Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West is backing the wealth tax proposal and says it applies to roughly 200 billionaires who have resided in California as of January 1, 2026, and could raise $100 billion. More than $300 million has been contributed to fight the billionaire tax, including two propositions that could block it if they gather more votes. Although stock prices fluctuate, Zuckerberg could face a tax liability of roughly $12 billion based on his net worth. In 2015, Zuckerberg and his wife, Dr. Priscilla Chan, pledged to give away 99% of his Facebook shares over their lifetimes when they celebrated the birth of their first daughter. The couple created the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative, a philanthropic organization whose efforts include curing, managing and preventing all diseases. Although Zuckerberg lives in Palo Alto, he also owns real estate elsewhere, including in Hawaii, Washington, D.C. and Ireland. Times data journalist Gabrielle LaMarr LeMee contributed to this report. articles.title: DOJ investigating Corey Lewandowski's role in DHS contracting under Kristi Noem
articles.summary: Corey Lewandowski speaks to the press in July 2024..(Photo by Andrew Harnik/Getty Images) - Andrew Harnik/Getty Images Justice Department prosecutors are investigating allegations of contract misconduct at the Department of Homeland Security, including the role of Corey Lewandowski who worked as de facto chief of staff to former Secretary Kristi Noem, according to multiple people familiar with the investigation. The probe follows a criminal referral for Lewandowski from the DHS Inspector General’s office, which has been examining contracting practices at the agency during Noem’s and Lewandowski’s tenure, according to one of the people familiar. The Justice Department declined to comment on the matter. “Mr. Lewandowski has not been contacted by the Justice Department regarding any investigation, and he denies any wrongdoing when he was proudly serving his country in a voluntary capacity,” Lewandowski’s attorney Adam Trigg told CNN. The Department of Homeland Security didn’t immediately return a request for comment on the matter. The referral is an unusual move for the Trump administration, which has been hesitant to criminally investigate its own members. Critics have instead largely accused the Justice Department of improperly targeting the president’s political enemies and accused DHS of protecting their own employees from scrutiny. In recent months, as the allegations of possible corruption emerged, Washington, DC, US Attorney Jeanine Pirro told officials in her office that she wanted investigators to look into claims of kickbacks connected to contracting at DHS, according to a second source familiar with the investigation. It’s still not clear which US Attorney’s office is leading the investigation. Prosecutors have been awaiting results from the DHS inspector general probe, the person familiar with the probe said. Lewandowski, a Republican operative, became a fixture at DHS early in President Donald Trump’s second term, serving as Noem’s chief adviser. But on paper, he was originally tapped to serve as a special government employee — a unique role meant to span a limited number of days. Lewandowksi’s straddling of senior government functions at DHS and service as a special government employee was uncharted territory, according to multiple people who spoke with CNN. Homeland Security officials ultimately viewed Lewandowski, a Trump ally, as Noem’s gatekeeper. He left the department when Trump fired Noem. Noem’s handling of contracts within DHS was one of the main catalysts for her ouster by Trump earlier this year, notably when she claimed that Trump knew of a $220 million ad campaign prominently featuring the secretary. During her tenure, Noem also tightened her grip on her department’s purse strings, ordering that every contract and grant over $100,000 had to cross her desk for approval — a move that Noem frequently defended as intended to cut down on waste but that multiple Homeland Security officials found unusual and unnecessary. The inspector general, Joseph Cuffari, complained to Congress in early March that Homeland Security leadership had been obstructing some of his work. Trump, when asked by a reporter on Thursday about the Lewandowski investigation, said he didn’t know much about it as he only just learned of it. He repeatedly said, however, that if people working for him are dishonest, he wants them prosecuted. “They’re stealing from me, so I want my people to be honest,” Trump said. “And if they’re not honest, I’ll have my DOJ go and do whatever they have to do.” This story has been updated with additional details. articles.title: Vivek Ramaswamy's $4 million attack ad against Amy Acton divides Ohio Republicans
articles.summary: A new campaign ad in which the estranged mother of Ohio gubernatorial candidate Amy Acton argues that her daughter should not be elected as the Buckeye State's next governor has added a new level of controversy to what was already one of the most closely watched races of the midterms. Acton, a Democrat, is running to replace outgoing Republican Gov. Mike DeWine. She's facing Republican Vivek Ramaswamy, a billionaire who ran an unsuccessful presidential campaign in 2024. In the ad, Acton's mother, Donna Arthur , calls her daughter a "liar" and urges Ohioans not to support her. "Don't let her become your governor," she says. "If you think she'll make your life better, you're fooling yourself. It will only get worse." As the ad began to spread across social media, Acton's brother released a statement in which he accused Arthur of siding with their stepfather after he was charged with sexually abusing Acton when she was a child, and criticized Ramaswamy for attempting to use the alleged abuse as a "political talking point." Ramaswamy defended the ad on Tuesday, telling reporters that Acton's account of her past "does deserve to be scrutinized." His campaign confirmed to the Enquirer that it will spend $4 million to air the ad across the state. The ongoing controversy over the ad, which has been widely condemned by Democrats and sparked pushback from some Republicans, has put a new spotlight on the race for Ohio's top elected office. Ohio Sen. Jon Husted, an incumbent Republican locked in a tight reelection race, released a statement saying he personally "would not have run" the ad. Meanwhile, Vice President JD Vance, himself a former senator from Ohio, said Republicans who disapprove of the ad should " stop whining " and remember that politics is a "tough business" during a campaign stop in Cincinnati on Wednesday. DeWine, who has endorsed Ramaswamy in the race, made his first public comments on the ad on Thursday, telling reporters that it was "wrong." "The ad, on its face, is deeply, deeply troubling, but when you know the rest of the story … it just makes it more wrong," he said. "It's wrong to run this ad." Trump weighed in on the controversy on Thursday, praising Arthur for her “courage.” “What she was really doing was saving Ohio from making a truly horrible choice!” He wrote on Truth Social. “The Press is trying to convince everyone that this Ad is bad, because it’s so good! Who wouldn’t use such an Ad? I would, it’s called, ‘hitting pay dirt.’” Yahoo Once a key swing state, Ohio has steadily become redder in recent decades. Four years ago, DeWine won reelection by more than 25 percentage points . But polls suggest that Acton has a chance to break the GOP's long run of control over the Ohio Statehouse. Here's what you need to know about who she is, how her past informs what she stands for today and what the polls say about her chances of winning. Who is Amy Acton? Acton has been open about the "difficult" childhood she endured growing up in Youngstown, Ohio, in the 1970s. On her campaign website, she says she overcame "periods of abuse, hunger, and neglect, and even wound up living in a tent in the middle of winter." In 2019, she publicly alleged for the first time that she had been sexually assaulted by her stepfather, Cledith Arthur, between the ages of 9 and 12. After Acton's biological father reported the alleged abuse in 1978, Arthur was arrested and charged with rape, according to contemporary news reports and court documents obtained by the Associated Press . Acton's mother sided with her stepfather, disputing the allegations. The couple left the state before Arthur could face trial and reportedly remained together until his death in 2004 . Both Acton and her mother say they have not seen or spoken to each other since a court hearing in which Acton testified against her stepfather nearly 50 years ago. "In the courthouse after they were charged, I went to give her a kiss, and she just turned her cheek away. That was the last time I ever saw her," Acton told the now-shuttered newspaper the Vindicator in 2019. Acton found more stability after moving in with her father and became a standout student in high school. She earned a bachelor's degree from Youngstown State University and a medical degree from the Northeast Ohio School of Medicine, working various jobs to pay her way through college. She completed residencies in pediatrics and preventive medicine before becoming a professor at Ohio State University , where she taught classes on maternal and child health. She also directed a community organization called Project L.O.V.E. to promote preventive health care among Columbus-area children. In 2019, DeWine tapped her to become director of the Ohio Department of Health. When the COVID-19 pandemic hit a year later, she advised DeWine to take swift action to control the spread of the virus. Under her guidance, Ohio became the first state in the nation to shut down all public schools. Acton also gained national attention thanks to the daily public briefings she gave throughout the early stages of the pandemic. In May 2020, an opinion piece in the New York Times called her "The Leader We Wish We All Had." Acton resigned a month later amid pressure from the Republican-led state legislature to sign orders rolling back COVID restrictions, moves she would later say "there was no science for." She briefly remained part of DeWine's administration as a public health adviser before leaving to resume working in the nonprofit sector. She announced her plans to run for governor in early 2025 and cruised through the Democratic primary in May. Acton was married to her first husband, with whom she had three children, for nearly 20 years before they divorced in 2008. She married her current husband in 2010 and became stepmother to his three children. What does Acton stand for? As a Democrat running in a conservative-leaning state, Acton fits firmly into the moderate wing of her party. Her policy platform focuses heavily on affordability, including proposals to lower the cost of health care, combat fraud, cut high energy bills and crack down on corporations that take advantage of workers and consumers. In July, she drew criticism from some progressive Democrats for saying that she supported barring transgender children from participating in girls' and women's sports. Soon afterward, she added language to her website pledging to protect Ohio's LGBTQ community, without directly contradicting her previously stated stance on transgender athletes' participation in sports. Acton has also spoken in favor of Ohio's voter ID requirements, a position that puts her at odds with many Democrats who view such laws as a voter suppression tactic by Republicans. Acton has also called for an increase in funding for police departments, more money for public schools and heavy investment in Ohio's rural and farming communities. What are her chances? Polling in the Ohio governor's race has fluctuated significantly as Election Day has grown closer. In the aggregate, the polls suggest that Acton has steadily widened her lead over Ramaswamy over the past several weeks. At the same time, two polls released in October show Ramaswamy ahead. The Cook Political Report and the Center for Politics , two of the country's top nonpartisan forecasters, list the race as a toss-up. No polls of the race have been conducted since the ad featuring Acton's mother became public, so it's too early to gauge what impact — if any — the controversy might have on voters' views of the two candidates. articles.title: California's billionaire tax heads to a vote, but 2 rival measures could block it
articles.summary: The California billionaire tax, Proposition 40, is finally coming to a vote on Nov. 3. The measure would levy a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of the state’s billionaires. Two competing initiatives on the same ballot, Props 41 and 42, are backed by opponents of the tax, including billionaires. If either garners more yes votes than Prop 40, it could keep the tax from taking effect. The labor union Service Employees International Union-United Healthcare Workers West (SEIU-UHW) is spearheading the campaign for the tax on the state's ultra-wealthy to prevent hospital and clinic closures, protect healthcare jobs, and help fund K-14 public education and state food assistance programs. Opponents, including Gov. Gavin Newsom, say the tax would fuel an exodus of wealthy company founders and investors, spark job losses, and further weaken California's economy. Read more: How billionaires get away with paying less tax What is the billionaire's tax? Prop 40 would levy a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of billionaire state residents, subject to the asset restrictions noted below. Taxpayers could choose to pay the tax in five annual installments, with a 7.5% annual deferral charge on the unpaid balance. Who would pay? Billionaire residents in California as of Jan. 1, 2026, would owe the tax in 2027. That's an estimated 255 eligible taxpayers, according to data from Altrata, a wealth-intelligence firm, reported by the Wall Street Journal. The tax proposal is not based on income — that's a loophole that allows billionaires to pay less in income taxes than the average American . Rather, the proposed California tax is based on billionaires' assets, including equity holdings, often in their own companies. The impact on the most wealthy would vary widely. A half-dozen or more high-profile billionaires relocated out of state as news of the proposed tax rolled out last year, so the number may be slightly lower. Those who have reportedly relocated include Google co-founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin, though neither has said that their moves were related to the possible tax. A Meta regulatory filing dated Oct. 21 said that founder and CEO Mark Zuckerberg told a special board committee that he was considering moving out of the state to avoid the tax if it were passed. The committee said it was "critically important to keep Mr. Zuckerberg in a leadership position with our Company and that he continue to reside in and manage the Company from our headquarters in California," and approved a special class of stock that he could use to pay any wealth tax due. The tax’s effect would vary widely. The Tax Foundation, a right-leaning tax policy nonprofit, projected that the tax would render Tony Xu, the founder of DoorDash, bankrupt, with a tax liability of $4.17 billion, unless he could challenge the initiative's valuation of his assets. On the other hand, Jensen Huang of Nvidia would face a tax liability of more than twice that: $8.5 billion. He told Bloomberg that he's fine with that . Read more: Where do millionaires keep their money? Who sponsors it? The California healthcare worker union, SEIU-UHW, launched the "emergency tax" initiative to offset possible healthcare staffing issues and service reductions at healthcare facilities. The union estimates a nearly $100 billion loss of federal funding over the next five years due to the passage of the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. How would the tax be calculated? Taxpayers and trusts with assets over $1 billion would be taxed on businesses, securities, collectibles, and intellectual property, but the tax would exclude real property and certain retirement accounts and pensions. How much would it raise? The California Billionaire Tax Act is estimated to raise about $100 billion, according to the initiative's website. The Legislative Analyst’s Office, the state’s nonpartisan fiscal adviser, estimates that the state would collect tens of billions of dollars from the wealth tax but says the exact amount is harder to predict. Where would the money go? BillionaireTaxNow.org says the money would be used to: Keep hospitals, ERs, clinics, nursing homes, and home care facilities open and staffed "Stabilize" healthcare insurance premiums and coverage Maintain healthcare jobs Fund K-14 public education programs and staffing Fund California food assistance programs Arguments in favor of the California billionaire tax The Institute on Taxation and Economic Policy, a left-leaning think tank, supports the California billionaire tax, saying that the One Big Beautiful Bill Act "cut health care and food support in part to pay for tax cuts for the very wealthiest Americans. The legislation gives more than $1 trillion in tax savings to the richest 1% of households over the next decade." ITEP added in the analysis that, "ultra-wealthy households have many ways to enjoy a lavish lifestyle without selling most of their holdings, and so can largely avoid the individual income tax. The billionaire tax directly remedies this injustice by taxing all wealth, whether this wealth has been realized as income or not." Arguments against the California billionaire tax The Tax Foundation believes the California billionaire tax, as drafted, contains "aggressive design choices and possible drafting errors" that could result in the proposed one-time 5% tax being "dramatically higher." It warns that "the poorly drafted initiative" could force company founders to sell "a significant portion" of their shares and lose their controlling interests. Stock prices could plunge, impacting retirement savings and investment account balances of working Americans. The Hoover Institution, a right-leaning think tank, has said the wealth tax would leave California about $25 billion worse off, accounting for lost income tax revenue from billionaires leaving the state. It also estimated revenues from the levy would fall short of the $100 billion projection, more likely generating just $40 billion. Read more: What is a high-net-worth individual? California voters will decide Nov. 3 whether to approve Proposition 40, a one-time 5% tax on the net worth of the state’s billionaires. ASSOCIATED PRESS What about federal wealth tax proposals? Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) has long advocated for a national wealth tax. His "Make Billionaires Pay Their Fair Share Act," co-sponsored by Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Calif.), was introduced in March. The national tax would levy a 5% annual, not one-time, tax on the estimated 938 billionaires in the U.S., estimated to raise $4.4 trillion over the next 10 years. In the first year, the bill would give a $3,000 payment to "every man, woman, and child" in a household earning $150,000 or less. The bill moved to committees in both the Senate and House, where no further action was taken. articles.title: Holiday hiring is heating up: Retailers and shipping firms are looking for workers
articles.summary: Holiday hiring is heating up with multiple companies saying they are adding temporary workers in the coming months, ahead of the holiday shopping season. Amazon announced it is looking to fill 300,000 seasonal part-time and full-time roles across their national support operations during the holidays -- an increase of 50,000 positions compared to the same period in 2025. Seasonal employees will earn an average rate of about $20 an hour. Shipping company UPS said it will hire 100,000 workers in the next few months, noting that many applicants can get a job offer in less than 7 minutes. John Minchillo/AP - PHOTO: A UPS employee unloads a truck before making deliveries, June 29, 2023, in New York. Spirit Halloween, the largest Halloween retailer in the U.S., said it plans to employ a record 52,000 associates at store locations. Patrick T. Fallon/AFP via Getty Images - PHOTO: The "Jack The Reaper" logo displayed in the windows of a Spirit Halloween seasonal holiday store in the location, August 26, 2024 in Los Angeles. Poultry company Butterball , famous for their turkey hotline, also said they are hiring their largest team on record to handle calls coming into their "Turkey Talk-Line" ahead of Thanksgiving. Hiring in September grew much less than expected, jobs report shows The October jobs report from the U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics will be released in November but data released in September shows that hiring has been increasing, although not as much as economists expected. Approximately 29,000 jobs were added in September, down from the 162,000 projected the month prior. Inflation has also been top of mind for concerned shoppers as unemployment sits at 4.2%. Teen summer jobs hit historic lows as fewer employers hire seasonal workers According to Indeed Hiring Lab , seasonal postings are up 10%, more than this time last year, but job postings for roles in physical stores have also declined. Retail job postings have gone up 61%, Indeed said, but other roles are also available with loading and stocking jobs up 9%, sales roles increasing 8% and customer service positions rising 6%, as shoppers continue to purchase items online. articles.title: 日本核心CPI年内首破2%，超过80%经济学家预计12月加息
articles.summary: 日本9月通胀数据全面超越日本央行政策目标，深层价格压力加速扩散，市场对年内加息的预期进一步升温。 10月23日， 日本总务省公布的数据显示， 日本9月核心CPI同比上涨2.1%，九个月来首次突破日本央行2%的目标 ，数据符合经济学家预期中值，较8月的1.7%明显加速。 更受日本央行关注的剔除生鲜食品和能源的深层通胀指标同比上涨2.4%，大幅高于8月的1.9%，显示需求驱动型价格压力正在持续积聚。 据彭博调查， 超过80%的经济学家预计日本央行将在12月加息，无一人预计下周会议将采取行动 。据路透援引知情人士称，日本央行下周预计维持政策不变，但可能上调通胀预测，并暗示准备继续推高仍处低位的借贷成本。据彭博援引知情人士称，日本央行可能在10月30日政策会议上首次表态，认为潜在通胀已达到2013年以来设定的2%目标。 深层通胀加速，服务业价格创七个月新高 本次数据的核心亮点在于通胀的广度与深度均有所提升。 剔除生鲜食品和能源的核心指标从8月的1.9%跳升至2.4% ，是衡量需求驱动型价格压力的关键指标，其加速上行表明通胀并非单纯由能源或食品等外部冲击驱动。 服务业价格同比上涨1.5%，为今年3月以来最快增速 ，较8月的1.2%明显提速。服务业通胀的加快被视为通胀持续性的重要信号，通常反映企业在劳动力市场偏紧背景下将更高用工成本转嫁给消费者的意愿增强。 商品价格方面，剔除生鲜食品的食品价格涨幅加速至2.9%。值得注意的是，大米价格同比下跌20.6%，创1971年有记录以来最大降幅——而就在一年前，大米还是推动整体通胀的主要因素之一。酒店、水费及食品价格是本轮CPI涨幅的主要贡献项，燃油税减免政策则继续对能源成本形成一定缓冲。 企业提价意愿增强，通胀扩散迹象明显 通胀压力正从输入端向消费端加速传导。据日本数据银行数据， 日本主要食品饮料企业计划在10月上调3153种商品价格，连续第二个月超过3000种，为2023年7月以来首次连续两月突破这一门槛 。 日本铁路公司（JR）宣布上调新干线“希望号”和“瑞穗号”对号入座票价，优衣库母公司迅销集团也在本月宣布提价，成为企业提价潮的代表案例。 第一生命经济研究所高级首席经济学家Yoshiki Shinke表示： “数据显示出上行价格压力的强劲态势。对于日本央行而言，这将强化其通胀依然强劲、超调风险仍不可排除的判断。我预计下次加息将在12月。” 彭博经济学家Taro Kimura亦指出： “日本9月通胀数据偏热，支持日本央行从宽松水平进一步加息。数据与日本央行关于潜在通胀正在接近2%目标的判断相符。” 加息路径边际收紧，终端利率预期上移 推动本轮通胀的外部因素同样不容忽视。中东冲突旷日持久推高燃料成本、日元疲软抬升进口价格，以及人工智能需求强劲带来的价格压力，正在削弱政府燃料补贴政策的实际效果。 日本央行行长植田和男此前已警告，上述多重因素叠加可能导致潜在通胀超过2%目标。日本央行上月将基准利率上调至1.25%，为31年来最高水平，并释放出防范通胀超调的政策信号。 据路透，Sompo Institute Plus高级经济学家Masato Koike表示：“核心通胀预计将因中东冲突推高能源成本及其二次效应而进一步加速。但由于价格涨幅并未急剧扩大，10月连续加息的必要性不大。”他预计 日本央行下次加息将在12月落地。 市场对日本央行政策路径的预判正在趋于一致。据彭博调查， 超过80%的经济学家预计12月加息，无人预计下周会议加息 ，12月加息已成为基准情景。 据路透，多数分析师预计日本央行将在12月将政策利率上调至1.50%，并预测终端利率将在1.75%至2%区间。 Capital Economics亚太区负责人Marcel Thieliant表示，日本央行下周将维持政策不变，但将继续就通胀上行风险发出警示信号。 “迄今为止的紧缩政策几乎没有迹象显示经济增速放缓，这意味着政策利率峰值高于我们此前预测的2%的风险正在上升。” 通胀前景方面，彭博指出，基于日本央行最新将本财年通胀预测上调至2.5%，结合已公布的实际数据，日本央行可能预计截至明年3月的平均通胀率将超过3%。 在政策层面，日本首相高市早苗内阁本月早些时候批准了一项法案，计划从明年4月起临时削减食品销售税两年，以缓解居民生活成本压力。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 5年消失25%岗位，照片冲洗员、文员等面临淘汰！高盛量化“新技术冲击就业”速度
articles.summary: 今年春天，AI取代人类工作的恐慌情绪一度达到顶峰。但随着美国经济展现出超预期的韧性，这股焦虑已明显降温——AI相关裁员公告数量从高点大幅回落，媒体关于AI导致失业的报道也退潮至年初水平。然而，高盛提醒市场：冷静不等于安全，AI对劳动力市场的冲击远未结束，只是在等待一个更合适的时机爆发。 据追风交易台，高盛全球投资研究在10月22日发布的报告中给出结论： 如果AI最终带来15%的生产率提升，历史经验显示，过渡期内最多约9%的员工可能暂时离开现有岗位；在技术让劳动岗位变得冗余的职业中，就业人数五年平均下降约25%。 当前影响仍可见，但范围较窄。高盛称， AI暴露度最高行业过去三个月就业增长较长期趋势少约1万人，不过这一缺口大体被AI相关建筑岗位招聘增加所抵消。 服务业横截面数据开始显示压力，AI采用率与失业率的相关性已转正且具统计显著性，AI采用率与就业增长的相关性略为负值，但统计显著性不足。 市场关注点也已转向投资回报。高盛称，当前资本开支预期意味着，AI用户每年需在AI应用上支出约1万亿美元，才能让超大规模云厂商和应用供应商实现市场似乎已计入的利润。对投资者来说，关键变量在于AI节省劳动力成本的速度，以及这种节省是否以裁员、离职和岗位消失体现。 1%生产率冲击：失业率短期上升0.3至0.4个百分点 高盛用三种经验方法衡量技术对劳动力的历史冲击。第一种是总量层面的技术冲击模型。结果显示，技术创新带来的劳动生产率每提升1%，失业率峰值会暂时上升0.3至0.4个百分点，约两年后影响消退。 失业率变化会低估实际岗位冲击。部分被替代员工可能较快找到新工作，部分员工可能退出劳动力市场，这会压低失业率指标对真实冲击的反映。高盛进一步拆分岗位流量后发现，每1%技术驱动的生产率提升，会带来0.5至0.6个百分点的累计总岗位流失率上升，同时拖累总招聘率约0.2个百分点。 行业层面的结果相近。高盛使用行业层面经利用率调整的全要素生产率冲击数据后发现，每1%生产率提升，同样对应失业率上升0.3至0.4个百分点，总岗位流失率累计上升约0.6个百分点，岗位获得率下降约0.2个百分点。 在高盛基准情形下，AI最终可能带来15%的经济整体生产率提升。按上述历史关系估算，AI过渡期内最多约9%的员工可能从当前岗位被替代，招聘放缓还可能对整体就业形成约3%的额外拖累。 25个职业样本：技术冲击后五年就业平均减少25% 高盛选取25个最容易受到AI技术冲击的职业，这些职业包括照片冲印员、校对员、档案文员等，属于技术对劳动需求影响最大的样本。高盛称，这类样本更接近AI可能影响最深岗位的上限情形。 结果显示，这25个职业在技术冲击后五年就业人数平均下降约25%。其中照片冲印员降幅最大，五年岗位减少接近60%，数码摄影和相关技术直接压缩传统冲印需求。 高盛样本中的25个受技术冲击职业包括： 1，照片冲印员，Photo Processing 2，电影放映员，Movie Projectionists 3，码头装卸工，Longshoremen 4，装订工，Binders 5，校对员，Proofreaders 6，保险核保员，Insurance Underwriters 7，档案文员，File Clerks 8，订单文员，Order Clerks 9，抄表员，Meter Readers 10，数据录入员，Data Entry 11，薪资核算文员，Payroll Clerks 12，计算机操作员，Computer Operators 13，排版操作员，Typesetting Operators 14，收银员，Cashiers 15，信件分拣员，Mail Sorters 16，货运文员，Shipping Clerks 17，打字员和文字录入员，Word Processing/Typists 18，电话接线员，Telephone Operators 19，办公设备操作员，Office Machine Operators 20，印前制版技师，Prepress Technicians 21，调度员，Dispatchers 22，旅行代理，Travel Agents 23，账单催收员，Bill Collectors 24，簿记员，Bookkeepers 25，银行柜员，Bank Tellers 这些职业的共同点是，技术直接压缩了原有人工流程。照片冲印受到数码摄影冲击，校对受到文字处理和拼写语法检查工具冲击，档案文员受到电子文档系统冲击，抄表员受到智能远程表具冲击，旅行代理受到线上订票渠道冲击，银行柜员受到ATM和手机银行分流。 岗位减少主要来自分离率上升，招聘放缓贡献较小 高盛最重要的发现之一是， 技术冲击下的就业收缩更多来自岗位分离。岗位分离包括离职、被辞退等人员离开原岗位的情形，招聘减少也有影响，但幅度较小。 在25个职业样本中，有13个职业的年度总招聘率下降，平均降幅为0.7个百分点。相比之下，有19个职业的年度总分离率上升，平均升幅达到3.8个百分点。 联合考察招聘率和分离率后，高盛发现，25个职业中有17个职业显示岗位人数减少更偏向由分离率上升驱动。这与总量模型和行业模型一致：技术冲击通常先体现在实际岗位流失，再体现在招聘放缓。 这对市场跟踪AI冲击具有直接意义。高盛认为，AI相关裁员应成为观察AI就业替代的高频指标。若未来AI带来的生产率提升兑现，单纯观察招聘计划可能反应偏慢，裁员公告、岗位分离和职业层面人数变化更能提供实时信号。 周期决定替代速度：经济放缓会放大AI冲击 高盛同时强调，AI对就业的影响尚处早期。美国只有23%的机构已将AI纳入部分常规工作流程，而且这一采用率仍会高估当前自动化程度，因为多数机构尚未把AI嵌入所有可应用流程。高盛称，大部分AI驱动的生产率收益仍在未来。 历史数据显示，自动化冲击带有明显周期性。经济健康时，自动化相关劳动力扰动通常较有限；经济转弱时，企业更倾向通过自动化压缩劳动力成本，岗位流失速度会加快。 行业模型显示，当整体失业率上升时，每1%技术驱动生产率提升对失业率的影响会比基准估算高出0.1至0.2个百分点。职业层面样本也显示，在技术冲击后五年内，整体失业率每额外上升1个百分点，受冲击职业就业人数会额外下降约4%。 高盛的结论是，若经济活动保持健康，AI劳动力转型大概率可控，冲击将逐步显现； 若经济进入周期性放缓，AI相关自动化和岗位流失可能加速，并放大商业周期波动。 对投资者而言，未来需要同时跟踪AI资本开支、企业劳动成本节省、AI相关裁员公告和宏观就业周期。 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ 以上精彩内容来自 追风交易台 。 更详细的解读，包括实时解读、一线研究等内容，请加入【 articles.title: 野村：AI增长恐慌取代通胀叙事，美债重获对冲功能
articles.summary: 美国国债与科技股之间的传统负相关关系，正在以戏剧性的方式重新确立。 隔夜10年期美债收益率单日暴跌逾15个基点，一度跌破5.00%关口，创一个月新低；与此同时，纳斯达克综合指数重挫2.60%，费城半导体指数单日跌幅高达6.72%。 野村跨资产策略师Charlie McElligott在最新报告中指出， 市场正在快速"重新定价左尾风险"——驱动力已从此前的通胀叙事切换为对AI驱动增长前景的系统性重估。 这一转变意味着，在过去大半年里令持有者"两头亏损"的美债久期头寸，正重新发挥股票组合对冲工具的功能。 McElligott明确表示，此轮美债上涨已不再是单纯的空头回补，而是市场开始将AI板块的抛售定性为增长问题，并据此进行对冲布局。高盛Delta One业务负责人Rich Privorotsky亦持相同判断，据其表述： "债券随AI抛售而坚定走强……AI的疲软重新定价了资本支出周期，并日益演变为一场增长冲击。" 行情转折：从右尾恐惧到左尾定价 仅仅两周前，McElligott还在描述一个市场唯一担忧是"踏空上涨"的环境。而其最新报告的标题已变为"快速重新定价左尾"。 就在48小时前，他在另一份报告中判断，美债的短暂逼空仍属机械性去杠杆，"尚不构成增长恐慌或衰退预期的叙事转折"。但他同时留下伏笔："我们完全可能在短期内到达'增长恐慌'的位置。"事实证明，"短期"意味着约48小时。 周四的市场结构印证了这一转变。标普500指数收跌1.22%，终结三连涨；纳指跌2.60%；道琼斯工业平均指数微涨0.02%，罗素2000指数涨0.11%。板块分化鲜明：日用消费品、医疗保健与公用事业领涨，半导体、存储芯片与光通信领跌——典型的防御性轮动特征。 期权对冲需求骤然升温 McElligott指出，数周以来市场几乎只有上行看涨期权的需求，这一格局在周四发生逆转。股票波动率、偏斜度与波动率的波动率（即"尾部需求"）均急剧走高。 QQQ隐含波动率曲线的变化尤为显著：前月隐含波动率从前一日收盘水平跳升约3个点至24附近，高于2月底水平，而一个月前前端仅在19至20区间。纳斯达克现货与波动率的关系也回归教科书形态：NDX下跌，VXN上升，两者重新落在标准回归线上。 野村交易台记录的当日对冲流量包括：SPX 1月5900行权价看跌期权成交1300张，VIX 11月25行权价看涨期权成交18150张，SPX 12月7400行权价看跌期权成交2000张。 QQQ 715美元这一关口的重要性在于：一旦跌破，做市商将陷入负Gamma区间，机械性抛售将自我强化。野村测算显示，若市场再跌1%，期权做市商、杠杆ETF与波动率控制基金合计需抛售约340亿美元；跌3%则为1340亿美元；跌5%则高达2250亿美元。而在上行方向，同一群体在反弹1%时仅需买入235亿美元，且在大幅反弹情景下，波动率控制基金的卖出甚至会令其整体仍为净卖出方。 美债重获对冲属性，利率市场定价降息 在利率市场，此次转变的意义更为深远。2026年大部分时间里，持有久期对冲股票组合的策略几乎是"双输"——股债同跌令传统的60/40配置逻辑失效。而周四，美债收益率降至近一个月低点，McElligott指出，美元利率波动率也随风险规避情绪走高，"美债终于再次作为对冲工具发挥作用"。 野村观察到的美国国债期权买盘包括：TYZ 108.5行权价看涨期权成交近5万张，FVH 106行权价看涨期权累计成交3.5万张，TYZ 107.5与107行权价看涨期权分别成交2.3万张与1.7万张。 互换期权波动率曲面同样印证这一判断：1个月到期、1年与2年期限的波动率单日分别跳升10.1和11.2个基点，而10年及以上期限几乎纹丝不动。McElligott指出，当波动率曲面的短端率先移动，市场定价的是美联储的下一步行动——在增长恐慌情景下，这意味着降息预期升温。 AI叙事重估：从Anthropic到Meta的连锁反应 McElligott将此轮抛售的根源归结为"AI轨迹重新思考"，并列出了一份详细的"起诉书"：Anthropic年化经常性收入数据令市场失望，并引发对其IPO可行性的质疑；Gartner警告超过80%的新兴云服务商将面临倒闭；多个AI生态系统相关IPO在全球范围内遭遇冷遇；Lam Research（LRCX）的业绩指引令市场失望；以及普遍蔓延的"资本支出增速趋于平缓"预期——尽管Meta维持了激进的资本支出计划并上调了预期。 Meta的案例尤为值得关注。McElligott以"向自身卖出看涨期权"来形容超大规模云服务商的当前处境：Meta在14C文件中承认，需要从今年秋季起通过发行新类别无投票权股票及大量债券筹集"数千亿美元"。这意味着超大规模云服务商正在通过向公众出售自身上行空间来为AI军备竞赛融资。信用市场已在定价这一风险：Meta的CDS利差从7月29日的80个基点扩大至10月22日的120个基点。 McElligott将这一现象定性为"非线性"融资成本： 当全球最具盈利能力的AI支出方都需要付出更高代价借款，其下游的新兴云服务商所承受的压力将成倍放大——这也解释了为何新兴云服务商是此轮调整中最先崩溃的环节。 增长支柱动摇，宏观叙事面临重估 McElligott指出，此轮抛售已超越单一拥挤交易的范畴。今年标普500涨幅最大的两个板块——科技与能源——正是他所称的"AI冷战核心约束"哑铃策略的两条腿，该策略年初至今回报高达60%、夏普比率达3。周四，能源板块跌1.7%，科技板块跌2.9%，两条腿同时折断。 更深层的影响在于宏观层面。McElligott认为，AI资本支出的涓滴效应，与G10政府的财政扩张共同支撑了美国名义GDP在今年大部分时间内维持6%至10%的"过热"区间，进而构成企业盈利增长预期的重要基础。 一旦这一支柱动摇，盈利叙事、经济过热叙事与"更长时间维持高利率"叙事将同步承压。 McElligott在报告结尾写道："此前关于'永久资本支出涓滴效应'的假设，已不再成立。"高盛描述的反身性循环或许能提供一定缓冲——收益率下行有助于缓解超大规模云服务商的融资压力，从而为AI交易提供支撑。但这一逻辑本身即意味着市场正在定价更低的AI增长预期，而在做市商于QQQ 715美元下方处于负Gamma状态、5%跌幅对应2250亿美元机械性抛售压力的背景下，市场距离真正的压力测试或许并不遥远。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 西部数据电话会：核心客户订单排至2030年，下一代HAMR硬盘明年上半年量产
articles.summary: 受益于AI热潮驱动的海量数据存储需求，西部数据2027财年第一季度营收大增55%且下季度指引远超预期，管理层在电话会上透露，核心客户的订单能见度已延伸至2030年。 华尔街见闻提及 ，10月22日美股盘后，西部数据公布2027财年第一季度财报，营收43.81亿美元，同比增长55%，分析师此前预期为41.4 亿美元。非GAAP每股收益4.64美元，同比增长161%，高于预期的每股4.11美元。 电话会上，公司CEO Irving Tan直言 AI本质上是一个数据系统，任何工作负载都会生成海量数据，这为HDD带来了比算力更具持久性的市场机遇。 Irving Tan强调当前，存储需求的增长已突破传统的核心云和超大规模客户范畴，加速向企业级环境、云服务商以及AI前沿实验室等多元化终端市场渗透，其 前七大核心客户订单可见度已排至2030-2031年。 针对市场对行业潜在产能过剩的担忧，管理层给出了明确的战略定力。 Irving Tan 明确表示，公司致力于通过提升磁头和介质技术来提高面密度，以此满足长期的供需增长，而不会盲目投资增加单位产能。 顶流客户订单已排至2030年，“物理AI”成新增量 市场高度关注AI需求是否透支，但西部数据看到的却是更长期的景气周期。 随着大模型训练进入深水区并向推理端和物理世界蔓延，数据存储正取代单纯的算力，成为科技巨头长期资本开支的核心。 首席执行官Irving Tan在会上给出了市场洞察： 关于AI的讨论大多集中在算力上，但我们认为更持久的机遇在于数据。AI本质上是一个数据系统。每一个工作负载都会产生更多的数据，而这些数据必须以可扩展和经济的方式被存储、管理和访问。 这种需求不仅停留在传统的云和超算中心，正在向云服务、AI前沿实验室以及物理AI应用（如机器人、自动驾驶）快速扩散。Irving Tan透露了令人吃惊的长单情况： 如果我们以排名前七的客户为例，我们在这七家客户中拥有直到2030年、2031年的良好能见度。事实上，我们看到需求信号在逐个季度不断增强。 针对物理AI带来的想象空间，Irving Tan特别指出： 我们在亚洲自动驾驶领域的客户正寻求增加需求，以支持他们的物理AI计划 。英伟达最近也强调了物理AI领域的收入机会在100亿美元左右。 如果你看到算力端发生这种情况，显然也有存储需求来支持这种算力。 涨价潮持续，Q1单TB均价跳涨28% 在供需关系趋紧的背景下，西部数据展现出了极强的定价权。 CFO Kris Sennesael指出， Ackerman： 谢谢。Irving和Kris，贵公司表示HAMR将在未来几个季度陆续爬坡。那么在HAMR爬坡期间，非HAMR近线驱动器的产能是否也会同步扩张？ Irving Tan： 我们计划在2027年历年上半年开始量产HAMR，与此同时，我们也将继续爬坡和供应最新一代ePMR平台。如我们所强调的，这一迁移推进非常顺利，实际上是我们有史以来最快的ePMR平台迁移。 本季度（Q2），我们预计40TB级ePMR平台将占所有近线出货量的30%；到2027财年Q3，这一比例将提升至50%，之后还将持续扩大规模。 因此，我们拥有两条强有力的产品线，能够同时向市场交付高容量驱动器，满足客户需求。 Ambrish Srivastava： 谢谢，Karl。今天只剩最后一个提问机会，请主持人安排。 主持人：最后一个问题来自Bernstein的Mark Newman，请提问。 Mark Newman： 谢谢，非常感谢，也恭喜贵公司今天的亮眼业绩。我想进一步了解定价问题。定价持续极为强劲，上个季度似乎还在进一步加速。贵公司谈到需求能见度延伸至2030至2031年。我想了解价格能见度的情况——包括已签署的采购订单或长期协议——我们应在多远的时间范围内预期定价保持目前的节奏？还是有可能进一步加速？ Kris Sennesael： LTA和客户互动中最重要的目标，是建立长期的业务能见度，确保在技术和产品路线图上与客户保持一致，提前规划好未来几个季度和数年内的产品迁移，并落实必要的艾字节产能以满足需求，这是我们最核心的追求。 在定价层面，LTA中包含一定的价格条款，但需要注意的是，存在基础量和超额量之分，因此具有一定的灵活性。此外，并非所有艾字节都在LTA范围内——时间越长远，被LTA覆盖的比例就越低，定价条款的约束也越弱。我们认为，在当前环境下，这种结构安排是最优的。 对我们而言，一切的核心还是技术和产品路线图的执行——做到更高容量驱动器、向客户交付更多价值，这为定价持续提升和每太字节ASP进一步增长创造了非常有利的条件。 Ambrish Srivastava： 谢谢，Mark。 Mark Newman： 能否追问一个关于艾字节增速的问题？本季度同比增速为22%，贵公司此前指引近线艾字节长期增速超过25%，竞争对手也给出了类似的指引。目前来看，25%这一长期增速目标是否依然有效？ Irving Tan： 我们给出的目标是超过25%。目前增速略低于25%，是因为正处于两次产品迁移之间。随着产品迁移取得更多进展，我们将超越25%这一水平。 Mark Newman： 非常感谢。 主持人：今天的问答环节到此结束。下面，我将话筒交还给Irving Tan做总结发言。 Irving Tan： 谢谢主持人。最后，我想留给大家几点思考。 AI投资的第一阶段聚焦于构建训练模型所需的基础设施。在这一进程持续推进的同时，接下来的阶段将是让AI大规模落地投入工作——从推理到智能体，再到物理AI。随着这一进程的深入，数据将持续复利增长，驱动客户提前更长远地布局规划，采用更高容量产品，并将其基础设施路线图与我们的技术路线图更紧密地对齐。 对西部数据而言，这创造了一个远超初始AI基础设施建设阶段的持续机遇。随着AI规模持续扩大，数据创建和相关存储需求将加速增长并持续复利积累。一如既往，我要感谢我们的客户、合作伙伴和西部数据全体团队，也感谢各位对西部数据持续的关注与支持。谢谢。 主持人： 本次电话会议到此结束。感谢各位参与今天的演示。您现在可以断开连接。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 售电公司持续亏损：批零倒挂的售电困局，20亿的净亏损，27年长协电价还要上涨？

articles.title: AI泡沫忧虑冲击亚太股市，韩股一度重挫4%，SK海力士转涨，黄金盘中跌破4000
articles.summary: 科技股抛售潮从华尔街蔓延至亚太地区，引发资金转移至债市与避险货币，市场对美联储加息预期也随之骤降。 周五亚太股市普遍下跌，MSCI亚太指数周五下跌1%，或创下连续第四周亏损。韩国综合指数领跌，盘中一度重挫逾4%，日本日经225指数亦跌近2%。 亚洲债市跟随隔夜美债同步走强。日本10年期国债收益率下行10个基点至2.78%，5年期国债收益率下行10个基点至2.19%，澳大利亚10年期国债收益率下行10个基点至5.164%。 在汇市，避险货币日元和瑞郎走强。美元兑日元下跌0.2%至156.44，周内累计跌幅近1%；美元兑瑞郎跌0.1%至0.8196，为近一个月低点。黄金未能受益于避险情绪，一度跌破4000美元/盎司关口，日内跌幅0.7%。白银跌幅更为突出，现货银日内跌幅一度达2%。 油价则逆势走强，布伦特原油攀升至五个月高位每桶114美元，中东局势紧张令能源供应忧虑持续升温。 韩国领跌亚太，SK海力士深陷多重压力 韩国成为亚太地区表现最差的主要市场。 韩国综合指数周五盘中一度重挫逾4%，后收窄跌幅，但10月月内累计跌幅已逾21%，成为本月全球表现最差的主要股市之一。 三星电子与SK海力士均一度跌逾4%。随后跌幅收窄，SK海力士转涨，三星电子则仍跌幅超2%。 华尔街见闻提及 ，SK海力士宣布暂停对旗下美国子公司Solidigm赴美上市方案的评估，理由是金融市场波动加剧，半导体股出现广泛回调，同时需重新评估IPO是否符合现有股东利益。 韩国金融监督院对Solidigm赴美上市是否违反该国双重上市规则也表示关切，金融监督院院长Lee Chan-jin表示监管机构正在审查此事。SK海力士强调Solidigm的投资需求不变，将继续探索替代融资渠道。 此外据韩国金融投资协会截至10月21日的数据，券商经纪账户投资者存款已跌破90万亿韩元（约合679亿美元），为今年1月以来首次。外资投资者领导了本轮抛售，10月已净卖出KOSPI股票130亿美元，抛售集中于科技板块。 三星证券股票销售交易员Roy Lim亦指出，随着券商存款减少，散户投资者对市场的支撑力度将受到限制。 Fibonacci资管公司首席执行官Jung In Yun表示： 投资者越来越质疑大规模AI支出能否迅速转化为可持续现金流，而油价上涨又增加了额外的不确定性。市场情绪脆弱，投资者优先考虑保住本金，而非逢低买入。 日本通胀超预期，加息路径添变数 日本股市电子元器件与金融股双双杀跌，半导体产业链走低。 周五日经225指数开盘下挫，一度跌超2%。日股消费电子与半导体供应链全线走低， 下游电子元器件巨头 太阳诱电 大跌7.60%， 村田制作所 大幅走低6.48% ；智能手机与电子零部件大厂TDK电子重挫7.30% 。 上游基础材料 三井金属 下跌7.81%领跌全场，半导体硅片厂商 胜高 大幅下挫7.73%，芯片切割设备垄断商 迪斯科 亦大跌6.34%，反映出资金对整个电子硬件制造板块的集中抛售 。 银行业金融股遭遇集体调整，大型商业银行 里索那控股 单日下挫7.24%，区域性地方银行 千叶银行 与 横滨金融集团 分别大跌6.24%和6.16%。 数据显示，日本9月核心CPI同比上涨2.1%，为今年以来最高，高于8月的1.7%，亦符合路透调查经济学家的预测中值。剔除生鲜食品与能源的核心CPI同比上涨2.4%，为今年3月以来首次升破2%，高于日本央行的通胀目标。 Ultima Markets资深分析师Elon Gu认为，由于市场普遍预期十月底会议将维持利率不变、十二月才迎来加息， 短线资金借通胀数据落地选择集中获利了结，拖累日本银行业集体走低 。 而避险情绪升温导致长端国债收益率承压，叠加对实体企业融资成本上升的顾虑，共同打压了银行股的利差扩张预期。 Capital Economics高级亚太经济学家Abhijit Surya指出，此次加速上涨值得关注，"尤其是在生鲜食品通胀大幅放缓、能源持续通缩的背景下仍然出现"。他还指出，尽管大米价格同比大跌20.6%，但这一急剧下降仍未能阻止整体商品通胀升至2.8%，高于8月的2.6%。 日本经济财政大臣城内实周五表示，政府是否正式宣布走出通货紧缩，将综合考量CPI、GDP平减指数及潜在通胀背后深层因素后再作决定，并称"认为政府正式宣布走出通货紧缩的条件尚未成熟"。 他同时表示，希望日本央行根据与政府达成的联合声明妥善引导货币政策。 避险货币走强，黄金与白银承压 汇市方面，避险资产分化明显。日元与瑞郎随市场情绪转向而走强。 美元兑日元周五跌0.2%至156.44，隔夜跌幅达0.9%；美元兑瑞郎亦下滑0.1%至0.8196，触及近一个月低点，隔夜跌幅为0.5%。 黄金则未能受益于避险情绪，现货金价一度跌破4000美元/盎司关口，日内跌幅0.7%。白银跌幅更为突出，现货银日内跌幅一度达2%，报53.51美元/盎司。 articles.title: AI崩盘终极推演：泡沫可能在2028年初破裂，科技股或断崖式暴跌40%！
articles.summary: 当前，全球市场正将筹码高度集中于一场史无前例的基础设施大跃进——AI投资热潮。然而，这场繁荣的底层逻辑正变得极其脆弱：当前的盈利主要依赖于科技巨头内部的“资本支出循环（Capex recycling）”和债务融资，而非外部终端用户的真实买单。 据追风交易台消息，TS Lombard首席宏观策略师Dario Perkins在10月22日的研报中称， 根据终极推演，这场AI资本支出狂欢极有可能在2028年初走向终结，并引发一场剧烈的市场重置。 报告指出，标普500指数将下跌30%， 科技股将断崖式暴跌40% ，约 20万亿美元 的市值将灰飞烟灭，美国股市的科技股权重将一夜回到ChatGPT发布前的水平。尽管科技巨头能凭借强劲的资产负债表存活，但AI生态系统上游的弱势群体（如新兴云服务商、独立模型开发者）将面临违约潮，预计将产生 1250亿至1900亿美元的信贷损失 。 TS Lombard认为， 宏观经济将陷入温和衰退： AI资本支出的骤降将导致美国GDP下降约 2个百分点 ，并造成约 80万个 数据中心建设相关岗位流失。但由于私营部门资产负债表健康且美联储有充足的降息空间，这不会演变成2008年式的系统性金融危机。 AI投资热潮：史上最大基础设施豪赌，可持续性存疑 AI资本支出已成为人类历史上规模最大的基础设施项目之一。 美国科技公司每年在AI建设上的投入约为1万亿美元，超级数据中心的累计投资规模已超越曼哈顿计划、阿波罗登月计划乃至马歇尔计划。超大规模云服务商（Hyperscalers）的资本支出占美国GDP的比例已接近历史峰值。 然而，这场繁荣的根基并不稳固。 当前AI生态系统的收入增长，在很大程度上仍是"资本支出循环"（capex recycling）的产物 ——一家公司的资本支出，就是另一家公司的营收。只要超大规模云服务商持续大规模投入，生态系统内部的收入就会持续增长，但这并不代表真正的可持续性。 真正的可持续性标志 ，应是来自生态系统外部——普通消费者和非科技企业用户——的收入占比显著提升。但截至报告发布时，这一比例几乎没有改善。AI的商业化变现仍是最大悬念： OpenAI和Anthropic约80%的收入来自仅1%的客户 ，而这些客户大多是依赖风险投资持续输血的亏损AI初创企业。 报告称，当前的AI繁荣本质上是一场“资本支出循环”——只要科技巨头不断向系统注资，收入就会增长。但随着债务成为边缘融资的主要来源，这种模式极易受到资本支出放缓的致命打击。 六大崩盘触发器：任何一个都可能引爆连锁反应 报告梳理了六大潜在风险点，指出AI崩盘已处于"过度决定"（overdetermined）状态——以下六大触发因素中的任何一个，都可能成为刺破泡沫的利刃。 触发器一：收入严重不达预期 多项研究显示，要使当前的资本支出获得合理回报，AI行业到2030年的年收入需达到 2.5万亿至3万亿美元 ，约为当前水平的 14倍 。这一增速在如此短的时间内几乎难以实现，尤其是在中国开源（开放权重）模型迅速抢占市场份额的背景下。普通消费者对付费AI服务普遍抵触，AI服务面临商品化风险。 触发器二：信用风险急剧上升 超大规模云服务商此前主要依靠自有现金流投资，但 债务已成为AI建设的边际融资来源 。仅2027年一年，AI公司预计将发行约 7000亿美元 新债券，其中超大规模云服务商占 4000亿美元 ，其余来自AI生态系统其他参与者——这一数字超过了欧元区所有政府债券发行总量。 更令人担忧的是"表外负债"的快速膨胀。以Meta在路易斯安那州的Hyperion数据中心为例：这是一个 300亿美元 的投资项目，Meta将其80%的股权出售给Brown Owl，成立名为Beignet的合资公司，后者融资 270亿美元 新债，由Meta提供担保（承诺租用该数据中心20年）。由于租约被拆分为五个四年期租约，Meta资产负债表上只体现了极小部分杠杆。 整个AI生态系统的隐性负债估计已达1.5万亿至2万亿美元 。部分新兴云服务商（如CoreWeave）的融资利率已高达 15% 。 触发器三："诱导利率"陷阱与折旧悬崖 报告将当前AI财务结构与2000年代初次贷危机中的"诱导利率"（teaser rate）进行类比。数据中心在建设期间无需计提折旧，但一旦投入使用， 折旧压力将骤然加大 。与此同时，AI实验室签署的多年期数据中心租约，在数据中心正式运营前不计入成本。一旦更多数据中心陆续上线，AI企业的财务状况可能在12个月内发生根本性转变。 触发器四：IPO浪潮揭开真相 Anthropic和OpenAI均计划IPO（后者已推迟至2027年）。历史经验表明， IPO浪潮往往标志着周期顶部 。更重要的是，IPO将首次为外界提供了解AI行业真实经济状况的窗口——目前AI公司披露的指标（如"年度经常性收入"ARR）明显经过美化，存在大量信息不透明问题。 触发器五：半导体周期与供应链风险 英伟达（NVIDIA）是AI建设的"镐与铲"，也是整个AI繁荣的晴雨表。 英伟达正在大规模开展"供应商融资"（vendor financing） ，向客户提供贷款以购买更多芯片，业内称之为"资产负债表即服务"。根据国际清算银行（BIS）最新研究， 超过55%流入AI企业的投资来自其他AI企业 ，循环融资特征极为明显。此外，半导体需求具有高度周期性，存在"牛鞭效应"——一旦需求放缓，当前的硬件短缺可能迅速转变为严重过剩。 触发器六：监管与安全风险 AI技术在公众中的形象持续恶化。 约55%的美国人希望放缓AI发展速度，仅13%持反对意见 ，且这一结论在各主要政治群体中均成立。根据2026年IBM/Ponemon数据泄露成本报告， 全球四分之一的恶意企业数据泄露事件涉及某种形式的AI辅助攻击 。一旦发生重大安全事故，可能引发强烈的政治反弹和监管收紧。 "二阶导数问题"：增速放缓就足以引爆危机 报告特别强调了AI繁荣的"二阶导数问题"（second derivative problem）： AI资本支出不需要绝对下降，只需增速放缓，就足以引发金融压力 。 这与2000年代初次贷危机的逻辑如出一辙——当时触发崩盘的不是房价下跌，而是房价停止快速上涨。在AI建设中，前沿实验室签署合同承诺向数据中心运营商支付数十亿美元，后者以此为抵押借款建设数据中心。但这些实验室本身没有利润，其持续支付能力完全依赖于不断融资。 超大规模云服务商的资本支出就像一本贷款账簿：一旦放缓，整个繁荣就会瓦解。 市场冲击量化：20万亿美元财富蒸发，信用损失可控 目前科技股占美国股市市值高达 40% ，半导体板块单独占比接近 20% 。美国科技板块当前市盈率约为 30倍 （一年前为40倍），远低于互联网泡沫时期70-75倍的峰值。在AI崩盘情景下，报告预测： S&P 500整体下跌30%；科技股下跌40%；其他板块下跌约20%，合计蒸发市值约20万亿美元。 报告称，这些估算将科技股占美国市场的比重拉回至ChatGPT推出前的水平。 到2027年底，非超大规模云服务商的AI生态系统预计将有约 5450亿美元 未偿债券、 9200亿美元 银行贷款和约 6500亿美元 私人信贷。AI相关债务总规模约为 2.9万亿美元 ，其中约 25% 面临风险敞口。 报告假设2028-2030年间累计违约率为 35% ，回收率为 25%-50% ，由此估算整体信用损失为 1250亿至1900亿美元 。这一规模虽然可观，但对美国整体金融体系而言并不构成系统性威胁。 股权持有人将承受最大损失（约20万亿美元），但不会出现2008年式的信用损失级联和全面破产潮。 最脆弱的环节包括：新兴云服务商（neoclouds）、甲骨文（Oracle）、独立模型开发商（OpenAI、Anthropic）以及建筑/设备供应商。 经济温和衰退，类似1990年或2001年 到2028年初，美国科技相关资本支出将较2023年上升约 3个百分点 （实际GDP占比）。报告假设完全逆转，但由于数据中心投资高度依赖进口，进口下降将部分抵消资本支出下滑对GDP的冲击。综合各种效应， AI数据中心繁荣结束将使美国GDP水平下降约2个百分点 （IMF最新世界经济展望报告得出了几乎相同的估算）。 报告称，整体而言，这场衰退的严重程度将与1990年或2001年相当，属于历史标准中的温和衰退，并给出了以下三个理由： 第一，私人部门资产负债表健康。 私人信贷增长幅度不足GDP的10个百分点，与1980年代末更为相似，远未达到次贷危机前的水平，不存在系统性信用事件的风险。 第二，货币政策弹药充足。 美联储自全球金融危机以来首次重建了充足的货币政策空间，有充分的降息余地，无需依赖财政政策大规模刺激。 第三，降息将激活"K型经济"底层。 长期受高通胀和紧缩货币政策压制的低收入群体、消费耐用品需求和住宅房地产市场（存在大量被压抑的需求）将从降息中直接受益。历史上，互联网泡沫破裂后，美联储的宽松政策迅速催生了住宅市场的新一轮泡沫，类似情景可能重演。正如互联网泡沫破裂后美联储催生了房地产繁荣一样， 降息将迅速刺激非AI领域的增长，这也是衰退将保持温和的核心原因。 此外，对于就业市场方面，报告指出，AI建设热潮目前已创造约 50万个就业岗位 ，预计到2027年底将增至 80万个 。若这些岗位全部消失，美国失业率将上升约 50个基点 ，在不考虑更广泛商业信心影响的情况下。 报告指出，最大的尾部风险在于： AI崩盘可能反而加速企业采用AI自动化来削减成本 。历史表明，互联网相关自动化的大规模推进发生在2009年经济衰退期间，而非繁荣时期。若AI崩盘触发大规模自动化浪潮，劳动力市场的冲击可能超出预期，导致缓慢的"无就业复苏"。 如何在泡沫中保全资产 报告称，AI崩盘是典型的需求冲击，而非1970年代的供给冲击（滞胀型衰退）。 长期利率将显著下降 ，债券与股票的相关性将转为负值，有利于国债的避险属性。但由于衰退程度温和，不会回到零利率或永久量化宽松。 AI繁荣与互联网泡沫的关键区别在于： 这场科技热潮高度集中于少数美国和亚洲公司 ，而互联网泡沫涉及欧洲在内的广泛发达市场参与。韩国作为AI供应链核心，过去12个月科技出口占GDP比重上升了 10至30个百分点 ，将在崩盘中遭受重创。 但欧洲等未深度参与AI繁荣的市场，在初期恐慌性抛售过后，将显著跑赢美国市场。这些经济体承受了AI繁荣的负面影响（高通胀、高利率），却未能充分享受其红利，AI繁荣结束反而可能带来解脱。 报告认为， AI崩盘对美元的冲击将远大于互联网泡沫和次贷危机 。由于危机根源在于美国金融体系，资金将流向欧元、日元乃至英镑等其他货币。全球投资者无需涌入美国国债寻求避险，其本国债券可以发挥同等作用。 报告明确指出， 现阶段做空美国科技股或大幅增加久期均不可取 ——若AI繁荣仍有数年可持续，过早布局将导致严重跑输。 最优策略参照GMO的Ben Inker提出的"易泡沫"（easy bubble）交易框架： 持有多元化全球股票组合 ，在繁荣延续时同样受益，在崩盘时跑赢集中押注AI的美国科技股。 仅在AI生态系统出现明显压力信号时，才逐步增配政府债券。 TS Lombard的这份推演报告传递了一个清醒而非末日论的信号： AI泡沫破裂不会是2008年，更像是2001年 。美国经济将经历一场温和衰退，金融体系不会崩溃，美联储有充足工具应对。 但对投资者而言， 20万亿美元的财富蒸发、科技股40%的跌幅、以及AI供应链国家和地区的剧烈冲击 ，足以让任何集中押注AI的投资组合遭受毁灭性打击。 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~ 以上精彩内容来自 articles.title: 2045年的芯片长什么样？英特尔晶圆厂实录：芯片会长高，每一步新结构都要熬十年
articles.summary: 10月23日，知名科技播客主持人Dwarkesh Patel发布最新一期特别节目。他在英特尔的晶圆厂和研究实验室走访两天，与五位技术负责人对话，话题从环绕栅极、背面供电、CFET，一直谈到英特尔与马斯克Terafab项目的合作。 这些对话指向两个判断。2045 年的芯片会继续往三维堆叠的方向长： 晶体管、连线、芯片之间的连接都在向上叠，但每种新结构要花约十年消化散热和集成难题，工程师自己对技术路线也只有约四年的能见度。眼前更紧的约束是设备：主持人提到AI算力十年来每年增长3倍，英特尔CTO给出的估算是，现有全球设备大概只够把先进制程晶圆产量翻一倍。 英特尔研发负责人：2045年的芯片会往上长，热量是躲不开的账 芯片靠晶体管运算。晶体管是微型开关，开合对应 1 和 0。给它的栅极加电压，下面的沟道导通；撤掉电压，沟道关闭。 器件缩小后，沟道关不严，电流会漏过去。办法是让栅极从更多侧面管住沟道：平面晶体管只压住上面，FinFET 把沟道立成薄鳍，三面包住，环绕栅极把沟道切成悬空的薄带，每条裹满一圈。 英特尔负责现有量产制程开发的 Chris Auth 说，环绕栅极早在 90 年代就是已知的终点："环绕栅极真正是最终极的晶体管。"前面的步骤没有跳过，应变硅、高 K 金属栅、FinFET 一路做下来，"你不会在必须做之前就去做"。 下一步是 CFET：电路里的晶体管分 N 型和 P 型，成对出现，今天并排放，CFET 把它们上下叠放，同样面积能多放一倍，代价是层间走线更难、热量更难散。 Chris 认为，到 2045 年结构会更激进。 "现在你面对的是一个悬浮在互连之中的晶体管，你就会想：为什么不是晶体管、互连、再来一些晶体管、再来一些互连？"存储芯片已经这么做了，NAND 闪存有了三维结构，他认为 DRAM 迟早也会走到这一步。 散热是最大的限制。他把限制算力的因素归为三件事：开关有多快，开关耗多少电，热怎么散出去。 三维器件让热量问题更突出："这会是一个限制，也将一直是个限制，但这些问题我们能解决。"至于何时落地，他很保守："我们对技术扩展的能见度大约是四年。走到那四年之后，你觉得还能再做四年。但如果谈十年，就很难说它会是什么样子了。" 晶体管上方还要叠十几层金属连线，把它们接成电路，这一层叫互连，现在用铜。 研究实验室的 Jack Kavalieros 等人在探索用钌替代：铜线要先铺一层衬垫才能粘牢，线越细，衬垫占的截面比例越大，钌可以直接刻蚀，不需要衬垫。他们说："在那些非常细的尺寸上，如果能拿衬垫的电阻去换没有衬垫，钌就开始占优势。"交叉点大约在 20 纳米的间距范围。他们也提醒，上一个节点选了钴，现在又回到铜： "当时领先的选项是钴，现在又是铜，将来也许是钌。" 芯片之间的连接由先进封装技术开发部门总监 Tyler Osborn 讲解。节目旁白先点出矛盾：芯片面积翻倍，边缘长度只翻倍，而芯片之间的数据交换靠边缘进行。AI 运算中，数据搬运的速度往往比运算本身更决定整体快慢。 混合键合是解法之一：跳过焊点，把两颗芯片的铜接口直接对准、压合、加热，让接口连在一起，接点就能排得更密。Tyler 给出一组数字：15 年前一级互连的间距是 130 到 150 微米，今天量产中的 Foveros 做到 25 微米，实验室里已在 10 微米以下，今年 IEEE ECTC 会议上有论文展示了 0.45 微米间距的混合键合器件的可靠性数据。他的评价是："我看到这里有很长的跑道。" 新结构晚十年才量产，英特尔给创新设了额度 FinFET 1989 年在实验室验证、2011 年量产，环绕栅极 1988 年验证、2022 年才由三星量产，这是节目给出的时间线。 中间要把约 2,000 道工序磨合到稳定，每周能在晶圆（切出芯片的圆形硅片）上批量重复，良率（合格芯片的比例）也要达标。 英特尔的教训来自 10 纳米（一代制造工艺，业内称节点）。Chris 回忆，当时缩放速度远超历史水平，又要在没有新工具的情况下完成，"这给流程和工程师带来很大负担"。他认为最该推后的技术是 EUV（极紫外光刻）："当我们开始定义 10 纳米时，结论是 EUV 还没准备好。"EUV 用 13.5 纳米波长的光把电路图案印到晶圆上，波长越短，一次能印出的线条越细。节目旁白交代了结果： 10 纳米原定 2016 年，2018 年才开始制造；台积电 2019 年把 EUV 投入量产，英特尔首个 EUV 制程 2023 年才出产品。 英特尔 14A 的外部客户决策正在进行，客户看重的是进度可预期。Chris 总结："我们学到的是，一个节点里不要做太多创新，因为创新越多，复杂度越高。"英特尔为此设了"阶段门"：新技术从探路进入开发，良率、缺陷、性能必须全部达标，达不到就推到下一代。 同样的务实出现在晶圆厂的会议室里。Kevin Fischer 在 Hot Topics 会议上要在信息不全时拍板： "你会学到的一点是，你永远不会有完整的数据集。如果要等完整的数据集，你已经等得太久了，已经太晚了。"他要判断的是"我们要承担多大风险"。 他举的例子是"外延节瘤"。外延是在晶圆表面一层层长出新的晶体，局部长疯就会形成凸起，让相邻部位短路、晶体管失效。团队"高度并行"，同时试多个方案，既加清洗工序去掉节瘤，也找源头。最高等级的加急批次叫 HotBox 1，在每台设备上都有优先权，Kevin 说："把高速公路留出一条拼车道，其他人都让开，只有这一个实验可以跑。"代价是"它拖累整个工厂"，所以工厂的人不愿出这张牌。 研究实验室里，新结构先做"短流程"样板：只做几道关键工序，测准了再拼成复杂器件。比如 CFET 先做上下各一条带子的简化版，"可能还不比现在的并排纳米带有优势"，但能先验证叠起来之后的接线问题。材料的淘汰同样直接，一种新材料可能因为"粘不上"就被判出局，或者后续工序的气体会改变它的性质，"如果找不到办法控制，对我们来说就是死路"。 英特尔CTO：算力要3倍，设备只够2倍 主持人提到 ASML 每年交付的 EUV 光刻机不到 100 台，要分给英特尔、台积电和 SK 海力士等。英特尔 CTO Pushkar Ranade 承认这是限制，同时说"EUV 或者 ASML 不是唯一的瓶颈"”我们看到所有设备都出现了严重短缺"。一个制程一旦确定，设备就被锁定："我们不能随便换一台不同的设备来做同一个制程。"他的缓冲办法是节点之间尽量保持设备通用，"从 18A 到 14A，也许 80% 的设备可以复用"。 当主持人问全球设备够不够把先进制程晶圆产量提高到 10 倍，他回答："10 倍不行，大概 2 倍可以。"主持人指出 AI 行业十年来算力每年增长 3 倍 ，Pushkar 说，除非整条供应链都多产，否则增不了产出。主持人归纳："产量可以在 12 个月内增加，但到 2030 年不会比现在预测的高多少。"Pushkar 补充了周期：设备订单"18 个月才能拿到货"，那就进入 2028 年，再要新建厂房，"基本上要到这个十年的尾声"。 这背后是代工业的成本结构。Pushkar 说："一座晶圆厂建成后，大约 80% 的成本是固定的。"线路和车站先花了钱，多一个乘客几乎不增加成本，所以每多一个百分点的利用率，都直接转成收入。他把行业的集中也归到这里：四十年前有二十家代工厂，现在只剩三家。 追赶台积电，他认为要补的是规模："我们需要追的是规模。"”如果你说的是技术，我认为我们已经到位了，也许在性能、功耗或面积密度上差几个百分点。"面对主持人引用的 SemiAnalysis 对比，他说："首先，我不认同你的基准测试。"他的标准是准时：可以差几个百分点，"但你必须准时"。 资本开支方面，主持人给出台积电今年约 500 亿美元、英特尔约 200 亿美元（台积电已把 2026 年资本开支上调至 600 亿至 640 亿美元）。Pushkar 认为这个比较不公平，台积电几乎是所有人的代工厂，英特尔大部分是给自己做，随着外部客户增加，开支会上去。 Terafab 是外部压力的一个例子。Pushkar 转述马斯克的想法："我们要么建 Terafab，要么就没有芯片。"主持人指出，工具是瓶颈，全球硅的总量不会因此增加；Pushkar 回应，电力、水、耗材可以扩，"工具不行"。 他还说，建一座晶圆厂的成本每 4 到 5 年翻一番，一台 High-NA 光刻机连同配套设备约 4 亿美元，这条曲线没法无限延伸。 他给出一个思想实验：研究型晶圆厂里让人吃汉堡、抽雪茄，看看良率会怎样。他承认没有现有厂商愿意这么做： "这是一个厌恶风险的行业。" 访谈最后，主持人建议英特尔像英伟达锁定内存那样大量承诺采购工具。Pushkar 答："如果早知道我们今天所知道的，我们会在大约一年前就多投入。知道了现在的情况，我想我们会投入更多。" 他还提到出售闪存业务："显然从后见之明来看，那不是最聪明的时机。"并认为内存的供给缺口比算力更大。 同一台High-NA光刻机，英特尔与台积电算出两本账 High-NA 是 EUV 的升级版，镜头的聚光口径（数值孔径）从 0.33 提高到 0.55，单次曝光能印出的特征尺寸小约 1.7 倍。图案太密时，机器一次印不出来，就要拆成两三遍分别印，每遍都占机器时间，也多一次出缺陷的机会。旁白算了账：一台 EUV 约 2 亿美元，High-NA 约贵一倍，能不能值回来，取决于能少几遍曝光。 Chris 说，两家公司对同一台设备得出不同结论，原因在架构。"我们用背面供电，这意味着你正面的间距要求会放松。"背面供电把粗的电源线迁到晶圆背面，正面只留细信号线，走线空间就宽松了，High-NA 一次能直接印出来。 他认为台积电没有背面供电，必须做更紧的间距，High-NA 做不了，只能继续用双重曝光的 EUV。"对他们来说不是很有帮助，对我们则很有帮助。"但这是英特尔一方的说法。 市场此刻关心的是成本。台积电董事长魏哲家 6 月在股东会上称，High-NA 尚未量产的原因纯粹是成本，9 月又有报道称台积电已同意从 2030 年起在量产中使用 High-NA。英特尔把它留作 14A 的选项，Chris 称会跟客户逐个讨论："它有价值，也有增加的复杂度。" 英特尔如今也替别家公司造芯片（代工），要向客户提供工艺设计套件（PDK），写明这个工艺能造什么、按什么规则造。Chris 承认，英特尔几十年只做自家产品，没有正式的 PDK 流程，"18A 一开始是没有 PDK 的"，客户反馈之后才补上，14A 一开始就按这个标准做。 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 老黄柏林“遛鸭”火了
articles.summary: 在2026年英伟达GTC柏林大会上，黄仁勋带着几只巴掌大小的机器鸭登台，现场上演了一场趣味十足的“遛鸭秀”。 这些迷你机器人不仅能够行走、转身，还能根据指令完成各种动作。黄仁勋甚至单膝跪地，亲自指挥机器鸭，但它们偶尔不听指挥、动作笨拙的表现，反而引得全场笑声不断。

articles.title: 暴跌之际，华尔街力挺Meta：投资进入收获期，五大AI“印钞机”已启动！
articles.summary: 暴跌之际，华尔街选择力挺Meta，押注AI资本开支进入收获期。瑞银和德意志银行在最新研报中均维持买入评级并上调目标价，核心判断是，Meta过去三年AI资本开支开始进入收获期，广告系统率先受益，五条AI商业化路径已经启动。 隔夜纳指重挫2.6%，费城半导体大跌6.7%，AI产业链承压。尽管Meta三季度营收及四季度指引双双超预期，但其AI资金承诺激增至8250亿美元，致使自由现金流十四年来首次转负。市场高度担忧巨额资本开支将带来短期发债压力，其五年期CDS飙升创历史新高。受此拖累，Meta周四股价大跌约7%，市值蒸发超千亿美元。 据追风交易台，瑞银证券LLC分析师Stephen Ju在最新报告中将Meta目标价从884美元上调至892美元，维持买入评级。德意志银行分析师Benjamin Black也将目标价从820美元上调至840美元。两份研报的共同判断是， 市场对Meta AI支出的定价逻辑正在变化，算力开始从成本压力转向收入资产。 对投资者而言，真正的分水岭是“兑现速度”。广告仍是Meta最硬的支撑，AI收入第一站也仍在广告系统；若Muse、Business AI、搜索广告、Advantage+和创作者聊天机器人带来的收入快于折旧和费用上升，AI资本开支将获得重新定价。若收入兑现放慢，当前估值将面临更重压力。 广告仍是最硬支撑 Meta三季度应用家族广告收入631亿美元，同比增长26%，接近总收入646亿美元的绝大部分。广告仍是支撑估值的核心基本盘。 拆分来看，广告展示量同比增长10%，低于2Q26的18%和3Q25的14%，显示量的增长边际降温。但单条广告平均价格同比增长14%，抵消了展示量放缓带来的压力。美国中期选举广告支出升温，也对广告价格形成支撑。 四季度指引继续强化收入端韧性。Meta预计收入730亿-760亿美元，中点745亿美元，高于市场预期736亿美元，且该指引已包含约1个百分点汇率逆风。 产品层面的AI改进已经开始进入广告效果。Instagram Reels相关性升级后，用户使用时长增加超过4%；Facebook新的生成式检索架构使Reels观看时长提升1%；Meta Generative Recommender使Facebook Feed部分定向场景转化率提升近2%；GEM扩展带来站外转化提升1.7%、应用广告转化提升9.6%；Andromeda改进使Facebook转化率提升1.4%。 广告主端也有反馈。采用Meta AI Business Assistant建议的广告主，在相同转化成本下转化量增加近5%，广告投入比可比非采用者高9%。瑞银提到，Advantage+带来的预算增量热度为年内最高。 AI开支开始被看成“收入资产” Meta估值叙事的变化，在于AI基础设施已压到广告主投放效果、用户时长和转化率上。核心广告系统已经在吸收算力和模型升级带来的红利。 德银Benjamin Black的判断是，Meta正在经历一个转折： “算力将从被视为‘成本中心’，转向被视为‘收入驱动资产’。” 这句话概括了当前多头逻辑：若AI基础设施同时提升广告转化、延长用户停留、支撑消费端代理和企业端产品，市场对资本开支的折价会下降。 Muse是关键变量之一。上线约六周后，Muse在美国和加拿大用户数超过1000万；已设置Muse的用户中，约25%会在任意一天使用。购物成为最常见场景之一，超过四分之一用户参与购物，平均购买金额超过200美元。 这意味着Muse的价值不只来自聊天使用量，还来自商业意图。Meta有机会在用户表达购买意图后介入推荐、比较和交易链路，再将高意图数据反哺广告系统，提升现有广告机器的效率。 五条AI收入引擎启动 第一条是核心广告系统。 Muse用于广告定向和内容推荐，直接影响“向谁展示内容”和“向谁售卖广告”两个关键环节。Advantage+则用生成式AI做创意和投放自动化，提高广告主预算使用效率。 第二条是Business AI和Business Agents。 它们与消息广告绑定，目标是提高WhatsApp、Messenger的使用和变现。Meta应用家族有36.4亿日活用户，同时至少有5亿个自我标识为小企业的主体使用这些应用触达客户、创造收入。若消费端代理与商家端代理直接交互，Meta可把发现、线索生成、交易、商业消息、广告投放和商家生产力工具放进同一张网络。 第三条是搜索和购物广告。 MetaAI/Muse如果能捕捉购买意图，就能进入更接近交易决策的位置。购物和旅行已经是Muse领先场景，商业化路径包括交易佣金、订阅、更高级模型或更多token使用量、面向企业主的付费功能、企业API与Muse Code。 第四条是创作者聊天机器人。 面向网红和创作者的chatbot可以拉长用户停留时间，带来更多可变现表面。逻辑类似Reels：先提升参与度，再逐步提升广告负载和变现效率。 第五条是企业端、API和算力出口。 企业端产品短期包括模型API、Muse Code和Meta Business Agents；更长期路径是把Muse部署到企业环境，并把Business Agents扩展到销售、客服等功能。若前几条收入兑现偏慢，Meta还可在供给紧张环境下出售多余算力或模型访问权。 兑现速度成为分水岭 瑞银并未把AI乐观情形完全写进模型。最新测算显示，Meta收入预计为2026年2562亿美元、2027年3173亿美元、2028年3792亿美元、2029年4406亿美元、2030年5037亿美元。 上修幅度相对克制。2027年广告收入预测从3045亿美元上调至3086亿美元，增幅1.3%；2028年从3613亿美元上调至3671亿美元，增幅1.6%。总收入层面，2027年从3143亿美元上调至3173亿美元，2028年从3756亿美元上调至3792亿美元，均约上调1%。 EPS变化同样有限。GAAP摊薄EPS预测中，2026年从29.28美元下调至29.04美元，2027年从30.81美元上调至32.01美元，2028年从31.08美元小幅上调至31.11美元。收入上修主要体现于2027年，2028年EPS抬升并不明显。 这说明市场真正关注的是“兑现速度”。 Meta管理层希望Muse从产品开发到收入贡献的周期快于过去约4年的产品周期。若AI收入跑在折旧和费用上升之前，资本开支可被视为前置投资；若兑现节奏偏慢，利润率和自由现金流将继续承压。 成本曲线仍重，2027年是关键年份 Meta把2026年资本开支指引收窄至1350亿-1450亿美元，总费用指引提高到1750亿-1790亿美元，其中包含此前披露的99亿美元法律罚款。剔除该费用，基础费用指引并未变化。 瑞银模型中，2027年和2028年资本开支分别达到2510亿美元和2996亿美元，股权自由现金流收益率转负。 总费用预测为2026年1754亿美元、2027年2131亿美元、2028年2662亿美元。折旧摊销也快速上升，2026年266亿美元，2027年458亿美元，2028年688亿美元。 德银估算显示，2027年运营支出约2120亿美元，同比增长20%，高于市场一致预期2040亿美元；资本开支约2330亿美元，同比增长66%，同样明显高于一致预期。 Reality Labs全年亏损预期为180亿至190亿美元。 效率改善是缓冲成本压力的关键。管理层预计，未来一年Muse计算成本效率将提升超过10倍，抓手包括模型蒸馏、提高GPU利用率、推理优化、使用非高峰或闲置算力、产品层效率改进，以及为特定任务优化专用模型。内部效率也在变化，每名工程师的软件产出同比增长超过一倍，超过70%的可衡量分析产出由AI辅助。 估值区间拉大，华尔街押注AI进入收获期 瑞银将Meta目标价从884美元上调至892美元，基于29倍市盈率，作用于截至3Q28的全年GAAP摊薄EPS 30.77美元。以10月21日盘后712.29美元计，该目标价对应约25%上涨空间。 29倍估值并不低。瑞银框架显示，该倍数相当于Meta长期GAAP摊薄EPS交易均值上方约2个标准差。支撑这一估值的前提，是Business Agents已经普遍可用，Muse已经上线且使用量增长，AI支出出现变现线索。 瑞银多头情形给出1206美元目标价，对应约69%上涨空间。 该情形假设两年收入复合增速提高到30%，4Q27-3Q28经营利润率达到34%，EPS为40.20美元，并使用30倍PE。 空头情形为539美元，对应约24%下跌空间。 该情形假设两年收入复合增速降至15%，经营利润率25%，EPS 21.56美元，并使用25倍PE。主要压力来自Class C股票引入后的股权融资担忧、2027年以后运营费用和资本开支框架仍未明确，以及广告展示量增速放缓。 对投资者而言，Meta当前交易的核心已经很清楚：广告仍是最硬支撑，AI开支正在被重新定价为收入资产，五条AI收入线开始启动。接下来决定估值方向的，将是这些GPU能否在广告、代理、消息、搜索和企业端同时产生足够快的收入回报。
